summary.tldr: Lets provinces withdraw from some federal programs if they have a comparable provincial program, and exempts Quebec from certain Canada Health Transfer rules.
what_it_does: Allows a province to withdraw from a federal program if it has a program with comparable goals, and still receive the same financial contribution it would have received otherwise.
Defines a federal program as one where the federal government pays money to help meet national goals in an area that provinces can legislate on.
Exempts Quebec from a rule in the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act that applies to paragraph 24(1)(a).
Exempts Quebec from the Canada Health Act rule on national criteria and conditions for the Canada Health Transfer, and keeps Quebec eligible for the full cash contribution.
summary.background: The bill adds a new rule on provincial withdrawal to the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act. It also changes the Canada Health Act rules that apply to the Canada Health Transfer.
